en: Where the series of distinctions that transcend one's own self ceases to exist, there is the Supreme Brahman, pure consciousness alone; that manifests as its own sole reality.

Oṃ. May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together; may we work together with great vigor; may our study be brilliant; may we never harbor enmity toward one another. Oṃ. Peace! Peace! Peace!
O Mahādeva, by a mere fragment of your compassion, I am Acyuta; I am a mass of pure consciousness, I am Śiva—what could be beyond this? (1)
Due to the expansion of the internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*), that which is one's own does not shine as its own; through the dissolution of the internal organ, Hari abides as pure consciousness alone.
Established in pure consciousness alone, I am unborn; what could be beyond this? Everything else that is distinct and insentient perishes like a dream. (3)
But he who is the witness of all that is insentient is the imperishable one, whose form is knowledge; for he alone is indeed Mahādeva, and he alone is indeed Mahāhari. || 4 ||
For He alone is the light of lights; He alone is the Supreme Lord; He alone is indeed the Supreme Brahman. That Brahman am I—of this there is no doubt. || 5 ||
The individual soul (jīva) is Śiva, and Śiva is the individual soul; that soul is indeed Śiva alone. A grain of rice may be bound by its husk, but in the absence of the husk, it is simply rice.
Thus bound is the individual soul (jīva), yet upon the destruction of karma he is Sadāśiva; thus bound by fetters is the individual soul, yet when freed from fetters he is Sadāśiva.
To Śiva who is Viṣṇu in form, and to Viṣṇu who is Śiva in form; Viṣṇu is the heart of Śiva, and Śiva is the heart of Viṣṇu.
Just as Viṣṇu is identical with Śiva, so too Śiva is identical with Viṣṇu; since I perceive no difference between them, may there be well-being for my life.
Just as there may be no difference between Śiva and Keśava, so too the body is declared to be a temple; that living soul is Śiva alone.

One should discard the floral remains of ignorance and worship with the sense of "I am He. Knowledge is the vision of non-duality; meditation is a mind free from objects; bathing is the abandonment of mental impurities; and purity is the restraint of the senses. (11)

One should drink the nectar of Brahman, practice begging for alms for the sake of maintaining the body, and dwell in solitude, becoming one who is exclusively devoted to the solitary state free from duality; in this manner the wise man should conduct himself, and thus he shall attain liberation. 12.

"May there be well-being for the illustrious Supreme Abode; salutations to the one of long life! O Lord of Gods, Nṛsiṃha, by your grace, people come to know their own self as Brahman—the essence of the Vedas, consisting of Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa, and Śaṅkara, inconceivable, unmanifest, infinite, and immutable. (13)
The wise ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye stretched across the sky. 14.

"The wise, ever-vigilant and full of praise, kindle that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. This is the instruction on liberation; this is the instruction of the Vedas; this is the instruction of the Vedas—this is the Upaniṣad. 15.
Thus ends the Skanda Upaniṣad belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
